Part A — grader and stakeholder review

The grader correctly rejects inconsistent ordinary pytest evidence, protects the listed control files, and gives zero reward for regressions. It does not establish that mutually consistent evidence was produced by genuine test execution: submitted Python shares pytest's process and owns its result files. That limitation is acknowledged in the docs. The current stakeholder changes improve disclosure, but do not fully enforce the reporter boundary: unsafe information can survive in requirements, several visible fields bypass sanitization, and the API deliberately exposes the patience tier. I would not treat the current combination as a strict reward/disclosure boundary.

This report is independent of Part B. Citations point to a frozen copy under /private/tmp/swesim-independent-review/snapshot/: HEAD a76654a5943f702ecb99ae6eb4413a4f8287da15, plus the working edits present when copied. The original checkout advanced during review; the source and artifact citations remain pinned to this snapshot. No repository files were edited by this review. The 28 local transcripts and three mirrored VM transcripts are historical stakeholder-v1 evidence, not live validation of v2. The version distinction is documented at docs/grading.md:243 and in the ledger at .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-12-swesim-implementation/progress.md:148.

Findings, ranked

A-P1-1 — Consistent in-process falsification is not handled (acknowledged residual). The result directory is chowned to tester; that process receives the JUnit destination and SWESIM_NODEIDS, loads the submitted roots, and executes pytest. The parent checks consistency only after it exits. A submitted import, repository plugin, or exit handler can therefore affect the very engine and evidence being trusted. Reading only the last terminal summary cannot authenticate its author. Established by code reading, not by executing a falsifying submission: swesim/verifier/grader.py:317, swesim/verifier/grader.py:369, swesim/verifier/run_pytest.py:12, swesim/verifier/run_pytest.py:25, swesim/verifier/parsers.py:65. The existing captured-output test establishes a narrower defense: tests/test_grader.py:156. Consequence: a coherent false pass can receive credit. Smallest honest improvement: add a control for this residual and qualify claims about forged summaries; actually closing it requires keeping the assertion engine and authoritative observations outside the submitted Python process. Another parser check is not a complete fix. The docs explicitly acknowledge this at docs/grading.md:121.

A-P1-2 — Demoting a fact does not remove its disclosure through requirements. ledger_violations(..., demote_unsafe=True) marks an unsafe fact author-only and clears its test links, but merely sets a linked requirement's fact_id to None; its text remains. Every requirement text then enters the stakeholder view and prompt. The runtime deny-list exempts identifiers present in those requirements. Thus a requirement repeating a hidden identifier can both put it in context and exempt it from redaction. Moreover, the draft sanitizer only checks discovery on-request and brief, while repo-derivable and volunteered-at-review are also visible. Established by swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:441, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:1283, swesim/stakeholder/view.py:28, swesim/stakeholder/view.py:40, and swesim/stakeholder/prompts.py:62. The test explicitly verifies that the link is cleared, but uses harmless requirement text "r", so it misses the disclosure: tests/test_swebench_source.py:1270. Consequence: the fact label's exclusion is sound but the information boundary is not. Smallest fix: validate every stakeholder-visible field, remove or regenerate requirements depending on demoted facts, and derive permitted vocabulary from validated reporter evidence before whitelisting it.

A-P1-3 — A2's worker-only patience-tier rule is contradicted by the API. Reply.public() returns patience_remaining and tier; the service returns that dictionary directly. This is explicit, tested behavior, not an inferred leak: swesim/stakeholder/session.py:118, swesim/stakeholder/service.py:207, tests/test_service.py:51. Consequence: an agent making the HTTP request can read the internal tier. The ordinary shim displaying only reply text would not change that API boundary. Smallest fix, if A2 is the intended contract: omit tier from public responses and adjust the test; retain only whatever availability signal the contract expressly permits. Documentation distinction: docs/architecture.md:86 actually says remaining patience and tier are public. The code matches that paragraph, but not the review's A2.7 requirement.

A-P1-4 — The general reporter stance remains partly prompt-enforced. The output filter recognizes a finite identifier list and only letter options (a)–(e) / option a–option e present in the current request. It cannot reject an ordinary answer such as “use the first approach,” unlisted implementation advice, or arbitrary verification advice as a class. confirm accepts any nonempty string within its size limit, including code; it is a channel convention, not a check that the input describes behavior. Established by swesim/stakeholder/session.py:45, swesim/stakeholder/session.py:175, swesim/stakeholder/session.py:233; the marker-based test is tests/test_session.py:295. Consequence: “does not choose implementations” and “never sees code” are stronger than the implementation. Smallest useful change: qualify these as prompt rules, restrict confirmation input to a structured behavioral description, and extend adjudication/filter tests beyond literal option letters. Full semantic enforcement is not supplied by a larger word list. There are no v2 trial replies on disk with which to measure residual frequency.

A-P3-1 — Timeout and forged-output prose overstates the narrower checks. The docs say diagnostic reruns use the remaining budget, but _diagnostic_reruns starts a fresh test_timeout_sec deadline after the initial invocation. This is still bounded: compilation deliberately budgets 600 seconds per invocation and 1,800 seconds for the verifier. The worked example “forges summary lines → outcome 4” is only true when the forgery disagrees with the other evidence. Established by docs/grading.md:63, docs/grading.md:108, swesim/verifier/grader.py:393, swesim/stages/compile.py:34. Smallest fix: document the separate diagnostic budget and qualify the forged-output example. I found no resulting positive reward from a timeout.

A1 — grader checklist and validation controls

“Control” below means a patch emitted by tamper.all_controls, not a unit test. That function emits only root conftest, startup-print, and, when a base test file exists, skip-marker patches: swesim/tamper.py:52. The sitecustomize function's name contains junit_forge, but its body is only a startup print probe: swesim/tamper.py:13, swesim/tamper.py:42.

Condition Handled at / not handled Relevant test Tamper control
1. Non-pytest summary text Partly handled. Captured text before the last summary header is ignored. Collection, JUnit, per-ID terminal status, counts and exit are reconciled. A coherent replacement after the genuine summary is not handled; see A-P1-1. swesim/verifier/parsers.py:65, swesim/verifier/parsers.py:111 tests/test_parsers.py:42, tests/test_grader.py:156 No
2. JUnit disagrees with terminal or exit Handled. Missing/unexpected/duplicate JUnit IDs, count/status differences and exit differences fail reconciliation; outcome 4, unknown observations, zero reward. Diagnostic reruns cannot grant credit. swesim/verifier/parsers.py:33, swesim/verifier/parsers.py:111, swesim/verifier/grader.py:571 tests/test_parsers.py:120, tests/test_parsers.py:128, tests/test_parsers.py:137, tests/test_grader.py:248 No
3. Submitted startup/config/entry-point edits Handled as dropped edits. conftest.py, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, *.pth, pytest INI/TOML variants, pyproject.toml, tox/setup config, and egg/dist-info trees are protected, including nested paths. Ordinary source changes in the same submission still run. swesim/verifier/policy.py:22, swesim/verifier/policy.py:214, swesim/verifier/grader.py:493 tests/test_policy.py:51, tests/test_grader.py:37 Partial: root conftest and sitecustomize only. Skip-marker covers contract test edits. No controls for .pth, TOML/INI, pyproject or entry points.
4. Submitted symbolic/hard links Handled by refusing members, while grading remaining regular files. Symlinked target ancestors are refused. A hard link already in the base tree is not handled by copyfile; unlink/replace writes or reject multi-link base files to close that residual. swesim/verifier/policy.py:88, swesim/verifier/policy.py:189, swesim/verifier/policy.py:234 tests/test_policy.py:28, tests/test_policy.py:74, tests/test_grader.py:122, tests/test_grader.py:143 No
5. Output above 64 MiB Handled. Combined stdout/stderr is read in 64 KiB chunks, retained under a bounded cap, and the process group/test-user processes are killed on excess. Outcome 4, zero credit, no flooding reruns. swesim/verifier/grader.py:44, swesim/verifier/grader.py:271, swesim/verifier/grader.py:364, swesim/verifier/grader.py:581 tests/test_grader.py:193, tests/test_grader.py:220 No
6. Repository pytest plugin Partly handled. Adding registration through protected config/conftest/package metadata is dropped. Modifying an ordinary module that an existing repository plugin imports is not handled; plugin autoload is not disabled. Protect/allowlist plugin code and disable unneeded autoload for that narrower case; arbitrary in-process mutation remains A-P1-1. swesim/verifier/policy.py:22, swesim/verifier/grader.py:326, swesim/verifier/run_pytest.py:29 Config/metadata tests at tests/test_policy.py:51; no dedicated repository-plugin execution test found. No separate plugin-module control; conftest is only partial coverage.
7. atexit printing after tests Not authenticated. Late stdout is included and a later matching header becomes authoritative terminal text. An inconsistent print is rejected, but coherent evidence replacement is not. Smallest complete fix is the execution-boundary change in A-P1-1. swesim/verifier/parsers.py:72, swesim/verifier/parsers.py:104, swesim/verifier/grader.py:369 No dedicated exit-handler test found. No
8. Submitted imports alter pytest internals Not handled. Importing trusted pytest before adding the repository prevents startup shadowing, not later mutation of imported modules or hook objects. Same fix as A-P1-1. swesim/verifier/run_pytest.py:12, swesim/verifier/run_pytest.py:25 Launcher manifest test only: tests/test_grader.py:396. No
9. Case/Unicode-equivalent paths Handled for duplicate normalized member paths. NFC normalization and casefolding drive both collisions and policy matching; archive collision becomes outcome 3. swesim/verifier/policy.py:34, swesim/verifier/policy.py:97, swesim/verifier/grader.py:499 tests/test_policy.py:62, tests/test_policy.py:69. The NFC collision uses the same code; the cited Unicode test directly covers matching. No
10. Test time budget exceeded Handled. Deadline kills the run and produces outcome 4. The 600-second initial and additional diagnostic budgets are distinct; see A-P3-1. swesim/verifier/grader.py:280, swesim/verifier/grader.py:362, swesim/stages/compile.py:34 tests/test_grader.py:260 No
11. Missing/malformed base-status file No such grader input exists. No-op really runs tests. Validation derives expected_base from the no-op report and rejects absent IDs or incorrect statuses. Missing report gives empty evidence and invalidation; malformed JSON/structure may raise rather than produce a tidy invalidation record. The schema's contract.expected_base field is not a required baseline file. swesim/verifier/grader.py:558, swesim/stages/validate.py:172, swesim/harbor_cli.py:74, swesim/models.py:87 tests/test_grader.py:62, tests/test_validate.py:175, tests/test_validate.py:198. No dedicated malformed-base-report test found. No tamper patch; no-op validation covers actual base outcomes.

The collector bounds and archives without following links and freezes in finally, including invalid or oversized trees: swesim/templates/collect.py:59, swesim/templates/collect.py:74, swesim/templates/collect.py:120. Its tests cover those paths: tests/test_compile.py:327, tests/test_compile.py:348. Validation requires every declared control, demands zero from incorrect-exploit controls, and does not accept infrastructure outcomes as defeated controls: swesim/stages/validate.py:24, swesim/stages/validate.py:153.

The protected-path and reconciliation sections of docs/grading.md mostly match the code. Its explicit residuals—coherent in-process forgery, pass-plus-teardown-error ambiguity, and pre-existing base hard links—remain real. The residual claiming the improved reachability probe is unmerged is stale: the paired-line implementation is already present at swesim/stages/validate.py:80, despite docs/grading.md:122. None of the three tamper patches tests the acknowledged coherent-forgery residual.

A2 — disclosure and session checklist

Rule Handled at / not handled Test / limitation
1. Author-only facts never enter context Structurally handled for fact records by worker filtering, service rejection, and prompt filtering. Semantic copies are not handled through requirements/other fields; A-P1-2. swesim/stakeholder/view.py:31, swesim/stakeholder/service.py:139, swesim/stakeholder/prompts.py:33 tests/test_session.py:181, tests/test_service.py:95, tests/test_compile.py:62
2. Test-derived facts become behavior Partial. Synthesized facts choose a safe gap text/question, else become author-only. This is selection/filtering, not a guaranteed semantic rewrite. The general visible-field gaps remain. swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:580, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:610 tests/test_swebench_source.py:1253 covers the seaborn leak, safe behavioral wording, and demotion.
3. Hidden-only identifiers trigger regeneration/redaction Handled for computed literal terms. The worker derives terms from test assets; one regeneration, then offending sentence redaction; audit stays out of Reply.public(). Identifier matching is case-sensitive; no semantic equivalence guarantee. Requirements/facts can incorrectly exempt terms. swesim/stages/run.py:108, swesim/stakeholder/view.py:58, swesim/stakeholder/session.py:54, swesim/stakeholder/session.py:179 tests/test_session.py:229, tests/test_session.py:256, tests/test_session.py:262, tests/test_service.py:266
4. Never choose implementation options Partial, otherwise prompt text alone. Letter-marker echo is filtered; semantic choices without markers are not. swesim/stakeholder/prompts.py:17, swesim/stakeholder/session.py:175 tests/test_session.py:295 tests literal marker choices only.
5. confirm-behavior only checks wanted/unmet behavior Prompt text alone for meaning. Code enforces length/nonempty input, review cost, common output filter and transcript channel. swesim/stakeholder/session.py:42, swesim/stakeholder/session.py:233, swesim/stakeholder/prompts.py:54 tests/test_session.py:328, tests/test_service.py:289; these do not establish semantic adherence for arbitrary replies.
6. Diff review only in diff-only Handled. Default config is behavior; both service and session reject review otherwise, before generation. swesim/models.py:199, swesim/stakeholder/service.py:180, swesim/stakeholder/session.py:239 tests/test_session.py:345, tests/test_service.py:309, tests/test_service.py:319
7. Fact IDs, tier internals and tool audit worker-only Fact annotations and tool audit are handled in response shape; tier is not handled, being explicitly public. Prompt-generated prose is not scanned for arbitrary fact labels either. See A-P1-3. swesim/stakeholder/session.py:118 tests/test_service.py:51 establishes the deliberate public shape.
8. Per-trial token, freeze, body binding, decreasing patience Handled for the deployed single-container model. HMAC binds the full session body including trial/spec/config; changed binding is 409. Frozen exchanges are 410 even for cached request IDs; body conflicts are 409. Positive costs, affordability checks and locks make successful exchanges non-increasing in patience. Failures/cached replies spend nothing. freeze remains idempotently callable with the token; it does not cryptographically revoke it for that endpoint. swesim/stakeholder/service.py:83, swesim/stakeholder/service.py:155, swesim/stakeholder/service.py:175, swesim/stakeholder/session.py:199, swesim/models.py:191 tests/test_service.py:31, tests/test_service.py:79, tests/test_service.py:109, tests/test_service.py:153, tests/test_service.py:379, tests/test_session.py:170. Persistence is committed before responses. Cross-container/redeploy coordination is a documented unmeasured limitation: docs/architecture.md:172.

The comparison uses the frozen selected brief in each trial's spec.json, not identifiers supplied later by the coding agent. These four trials all predate stakeholder v2. Some method/file names occur in the original traceback and are therefore not independently leaks. The entries above identify additional names, test construction, verification instructions, or explicit choices; an unverified-review disclaimer does not make that information reporter knowledge. The ledger records that these earlier replies triggered the current fix, and the docs properly warn against using their success correlation as evidence of a treatment effect: .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-12-swesim-implementation/progress.md:148, docs/grading.md:243.

Checks and limits

  • The requested initial offline suite: 525 passed, 6 skipped, 6 failed, all six failures from sandbox-denied localhost bind() in service/shim tests. The prompt's “one socket test” description is outdated.
  • The authorized bash scripts/verify.sh 10 rerun with localhost access: 444 selected tests passed, VERIFY OK through M10, and its final full suite reported 544 passed. The differing suite count reflects the concurrent checkout changes; these are execution results, not a claim that the moving checkout was an immutable test target.
  • Built the tracked seaborn verifier Dockerfile for linux/amd64 on the local ARM Docker host. Replayed the tracked successful submission with --network none: outcome 1, reward 1, F2P 1/1, P2P 84/84. Results: local reward, local report. The regression replay produced outcome 2, reward 0, F2P 1/1, P2P 79/84: local regression report.
  • The Docker inputs reconstructed the applied diffs against the image's pristine tree and used the project collector to produce a new local root receipt. This tests offline grading of those code changes; it does not reproduce the original Harbor collection lifecycle, protected edits omitted from the applied diff, or remote transcript freeze.
  • No cloud jobs, live stakeholder calls, coherent-forgery submission, or multi-container restart experiment was run. No v2 interaction outcomes are available in the reviewed artifacts. The tables explicitly distinguish tested checks, code-reading conclusions and prompt-only rules.
